title.zh: 卷五十九 表第一: 宗室表
title.raw: 卷五十九 表第一: 宗室表 Volume 59 Tables 1: Imperial Family

sentences.zh: 古者太史掌敘邦國之世次，辨其姓氏，別其昭穆，尚失。

translations.literal: In antiquity the Grand Historian kept the generations of the states, distinguished their surnames, and separated zhao from mu—and still there were lapses.
translations.idiomatic: Even in ancient times the Grand Historian who ordered the ages of the realms, sorted clan names, and marked senior from junior lines could not keep the record whole.

sentences.zh: 金人初起完毅十二部，其後皆以部為氏，史臣記錄有稱「宗室」者，有稱完顏者。

translations.literal: When the Jin people first arose in the twelve tribes of Wanyi, afterward all took their tribe as surname; in the historians' records some are called 「Imperial Clan」, some Wanyan.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin first gathered in the twelve Wanyi tribes, then took each tribe as a clan name. Court historians sometimes wrote 「Imperial Clan」, sometimes Wanyan.

translations.literal: Those called Wanyan.
translations.idiomatic: As for those called Wanyan:

sentences.zh: 稱完顏者亦有二焉，有同姓完顏，蓋疏族，若石土門、迪古乃是也；

translations.literal: Those called Wanyan also fall into two kinds: same-surname Wanyan, who were in fact collateral kin—Shitumen and Digunai are examples;
translations.idiomatic: 「Wanyan」 itself split two ways: same-surname Wanyan were really distant kin, men like Shitumen and Digunai;

sentences.zh: 有異姓完顏，蓋部人，若歡都是也。

translations.literal: and different-surname Wanyan, who were in fact men of the tribe—Huandu is an example.
translations.idiomatic: different-surname Wanyan were really tribesmen, men like Huandu.

sentences.zh: 大定以前稱「宗室」，明昌以後避睿宗諱稱「內族」，其實一而已，書名不書氏，其制如此。

translations.literal: Before the Dading era they were called 「Imperial Clan」; after Mingchang, to avoid the taboo on Ruizong they were called 「Inner Kin」—in substance one and the same. The annals give personal names, not clan names; such was the rule.
translations.idiomatic: Before Dading the phrase was 「Imperial Clan」; after Mingchang, honoring Ruizong's name, 「Inner Kin」—one body of people either way. Registers record given names, not surnames, by established custom.

sentences.zh: 宣宗詔宗室皆稱完顏，不復識別焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong decreed that all of the imperial clan should be called Wanyan, and no further distinction was made.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong ordered every member of the clan to bear the name Wanyan, and the old categories were dropped.

sentences.zh: 大定、泰和之間，袒免以上親皆有屬籍，以敘授官，大功以上，薨卒輟朝，親親之道行焉。

translations.literal: Between Dading and Taihe, kin within the degree of tan-mian mourning and closer all had household registers, by which offices were assigned; for kin within the degree of da-gong mourning and closer, death halted court audiences—the way of cherishing kin was practiced.
translations.idiomatic: From Dading through Taihe, relatives within tan-mian degree and nearer were entered in the clan rolls and ranked for appointment; when one within da-gong degree or nearer died, court paused in mourning—kinship was honored in deed.

sentences.zh: 貞祐以後，譜牒散失，大概僅存，不可殫悉，今掇其可次第者著於篇。

translations.literal: After Zhenyou the genealogical registers were scattered and lost; only a rough outline survives, and it cannot be set forth in full. Now I gather what can be ordered by generation and set it down in this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhenyou the pedigree books were lost; a broken outline alone remains, too fragmentary to exhaust. Here I collect what can still be sequenced and place it in these pages.

sentences.zh: 其上無所系、下無所承者，不能盡錄也。

translations.literal: Those with no tie above and no succession below cannot all be recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Lines that attach to nothing above and hand down to nothing below cannot be entered in full.

cells.content: 銀术可（拔離族子。同中書門下平章事。）
cells.literal: Yinshuake (kinsman of the Balisu clan; Fellow Associate Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery).
cells.idiomatic: Yinshuake (kinsman of the Balisu clan; Fellow Associate Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery).

cells.content: 麻吉（銀术可弟。銀青光祿大夫。）
cells.literal: Maji (younger brother of Yinshuake; Silver Radiance Grand Master of Splendid Happiness).
cells.idiomatic: Maji (younger brother of Yinshuake; Silver Radiance Grand Master of Splendid Happiness).

cells.content: 宗賢（本名阿魯。太祖從姪。婆速路兵馬都緫管。）
cells.literal: Zongxian (born Alu; Taizu's nephew by the collateral line; Commander of the Bosu-route military).
cells.idiomatic: Zongxian (born Alu; Taizu's nephew by the collateral line; Commander of the Bosu-route military).

sentences.zh: 右諸宗室可譜者凡十一族，雖稱系出某帝，而不能世次，不譜於各帝之下，所以慎也。

translations.literal: At right: of the imperial kin who can be entered in a pedigree, eleven clans in all; though they are said to stem from a given emperor, their generations cannot be fixed, so they are not entered under each emperor's line — hence the caution.
translations.idiomatic: Listed at right: of the imperial kin who can still be charted, eleven clans in all; though each line is said to descend from a given emperor, the generations cannot be fixed, so they are not entered under each emperor's sons — that is why the record is cautious.
